newsitem.title: USA: CME hopes to trade South African rand derivatives.
newsitem.headline: CME hopes to trade South African rand derivatives.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said Monday it had filed for regulatory approval to trade futures and options on the South African rand.
The proposed contracts would be sized at 500,000 rand, equal to roughly $107,000 at current levels, the exchange said. They would be quoted in U.S. dollars per rand.

The exchange said it plans to trade futures expiring in the March quarterly cycle, with settlement by physical delivery. Quarterly and serial month options on rand futures contracts would also be offered. A start date would be set pending Commodity Futures Trading Commission approval, it said. ((Chicago derivatives desk, 312 408-8750; Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
